description: Hey! We're Team Sehnsucht—a two-person crew mixing junior tech energy with life sciences to build something awesome for this challenge. We're all about coding, AI, and turning wild space ideas into reality. Let's make it happen!
summary:
SOL 7 is a first-person Mars survival game for ages 7-12, built by Team Sehnsucht. Players launch from Earth, fly their own landing, salvage the capsule, melt ice for water, grow potatoes, build a base, and survive a dust storm and a meteor shower. By Sol 7, they unlock data chips and program the capsule to fly home. It is a free Windows app.

It answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning real trade-offs into gameplay: oxygen, water, food, power and radiation compete, and no choice is free. Values come from public NASA data, credited in-game, and subtitles explain every science term.

It matters because kids learn how astronauts actually survive through play, not posters, and every failure teaches something real.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS SOL 7 is a first-person Mars survival game and mission trainer for ages 7-12. SOL 7 can be played two ways: free in the browser (no download or account), or as a Windows app from our GitHub release. It runs on desktop browsers with WebGL, and Chrome or Edge work best. The player is a stranded astronaut of the fictional Huraira Meerab Space Agency (HMSA) and must survive seven Sols on Mars and get home.
The player launches from Earth and flies the lander through a retro-propulsive landing, using thrust, tilt and fine RCS controls. A crash means retrying. After landing at the Jezero Crater site, the player salvages the descent stage, scoops water ice and melts it in a solar-powered crucible, breaks rocks with a hammer, and manages a backpack and hotbar. A crafting table unlocks a blueprint hologram of a modular research base: airlock, living quarters, greenhouse, storage and power station. Inside, they plant, water and harvest potatoes, use the monitoring screens (weather, power, communications and life support), and craft RTGs for power.
Each Sol brings a new problem. A dust storm damages the solar panels, a long cold night makes the outside deadly, a global isolation storm blocks the sun, and a meteor shower hits. Each Sol is about five minutes of daylight. At night the player must be inside the base or they freeze. By Sol 6, Mission Control sends the data chips needed for the trip home. The player connects an RTG to the return capsule, loads the last data chip, and launches on Sol 7. There is no rescue ship, so the player earns the ending.
BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT Players feel real mission trade-offs instead of reading about them. Oxygen, water, food, power and radiation all compete, so no choice is free. Spending ice on water or on crafting, or time on repairs or farming, has consequences that build over the Sols. Failure is a lesson: the game shows why it happened, and the player retries right away. Subtitles define each science term (sol, RTG, MOXIE and others) the first time it appears, so a child needs no background knowledge. We hope players leave understanding why spaceflight is hard and curious about careers in space science.
REAL DATA The game's values come from public NASA data and are built into the game as reference numbers. They are not a live feed. They cover Martian gravity (3.71 m/s2), radiation, surface weather and pressure, the Jezero landing site, MOXIE oxygen production, and the real sizes of Phobos and Deimos. An in-game credits screen and our repository's credits file list every source.
TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY JavaScript (ES modules), Three.js for 3D graphics, GLSL shaders for the Mars globe and sky, HTML and CSS for the interface, the Web Audio API for sound, Electron and electron-builder for the Windows app, Visual Studio Code, and Git and GitHub. The code is open source on GitHub, and the game runs offline and collects no data.
HOW IT IS CREATIVE SOL 7 is a story the player lives through. They fly, build, farm and repair, and every Sol feels different. The fictional HMSA frames the mission. All art, terrain, skies, moons and music are generated by code, with no outside art or audio files. The night sky shows Phobos and Deimos at their true sizes, and the base screens show live-style telemetry.
FACTORS WE CONSIDERED Age-appropriate language, a difficulty that is hard but fair, scientific accuracy, clear data credits, and a simple download that needs no account. We kept the number of core systems small so young players are not overwhelmed, and we made every failure a learning moment.
